newsitem.title: BELGIUM: BELGIUM BRACES FOR STRIKES ON MONDAY.
newsitem.headline: BELGIUM BRACES FOR STRIKES ON MONDAY.

text.p: Belgium is bracing for a wave of strikes on Monday as private and public sector unions and a major rail union stop work for reasons ranging from wage talks to pensions.
The 24-hour rail stoppage, announced by Belgian railways on Friday, begins at 2200 (2100 GMT) on Sunday. SNCB said it expected serious disruption to rail traffic.

Rail unions are worried about the future of state pensions and policy on state companies as Belgium tightens its budgetary belt in preparation for joining the European Union's single currency in 1999.
The ABVV/FGTB private and public sector unions will also hold a 24-hour strike on Monday in a pre-emptive bid to get the most out of what scarce scope there is for wage increases and job creation.
It is not clear how widely the strike call will be followed.
